chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt upon people, and the zakat is withheld in it. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no zakat upon him regarding it until he takes possession of it. So when he takes possession of it, then upon him is the zakat. And if its withholding is prolonged by the people until complete years pass, so there is no zakat upon him until it comes out (to him). So when it comes out, he pays the zakat for that year of his. And if he was taking from it little by little, let him purify (pay zakat) what comes out from it first, then first.

And if his chattels, and his debts, and his wealth are in his business in which he moves day by day, taking and giving, selling and buying, so it is like the principal in his hand, so upon him is the zakat. And it is not befitting for him to change that when the state of his chattels and his wealth is upon what I have described to you, so he delays the zakat.
ai.seo_question: When is zakat due on debts owed by people?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that zakat on debts is deferred until actual receipt, with Samaanah specifying that prolonged non-payment does not accumulate multiple years' dues, only the year of collection. It further distinguishes between personal debts and commercial capital, ruling that if debt is integral to daily trading activities, it is treated as liquid wealth subject to immediate zakat, preventing artificial deferral. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the actual possession of wealth (qabd) as the trigger for zakat liability.
